json.name: ha_history_get_current_time
json.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Oslo).
Call this before time-based queries that use relative or named periods such as
"last month", "this winter", "yesterday", or "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

json.name: ha_history_list_areas
json.description:
Lists the areas (rooms and locations) defined in Oslo.
Use when the user wants to explore areas or when you need the exact area name for ha_history_list_devices.
Narrow by name with search. Returns area names to reuse with area="<name>" in ha_history_list_devices, which also surfaces ready entity_ids.

search.description:
Optional search term matched against area names (case-insensitive substring match).
E.g. "kitchen", "outdoor", "bedroom". Leave empty to list all areas.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: all areas.

json.name: ha_history_list_devices
json.description:
Lists devices in Oslo, filtered by area or search.
Use area for room-based discovery and search for device or appliance lookup.
Returns matched devices together with analytics-ready entity_ids on each device.
Use the returned entity_ids directly with the analytics tools. Call ha_history_list_device_entities only when you need deeper per-device inspection.

area.description:
Filter by area name (case-insensitive). Use the area name from ha_history_list_areas.
Leave empty to list all devices across all areas.

search.description:
Optional search term matched against device names (case-insensitive substring match).
E.g. "charger", "climate", "motion". Returns devices whose name contains the term.

include_disabled.description: When true, includes disabled devices. Default: false.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: unlimited when search or area is provided. When omitted with no filters, the call is blocked and you must provide a filter.

json.name: ha_history_list_device_entities
json.description:
Lists entities (sensors and controls) on a specific device in Oslo.
Use when ha_history_list_devices did not already surface the needed entity_ids or when you need a deeper per-device inspection.
Returns entity_ids with their metric kind and analytics capability.
Use measurement sensors with ha_history_get_sensor_stats and cumulative counters with ha_history_get_consumption.

device.description:
Device name (case-insensitive). Use the device name from ha_history_list_devices.
Partial name match is supported, e.g. "car charging" matches "Car Charging Plug".

metric.description:
Optional metric type to filter entities. Supported values:
"power", "energy", "temperature", "humidity", "motion", "presence".
Leave empty to show all analytics-capable entities on the device.

include_diagnostics.description: When true, includes diagnostic and config entities. Default: false.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 20.

json.name: ha_history_list_entities
json.description:
Primary discovery tool for exact entity_ids. Filter by area, device, device_class, and search.
Results are grouped by area and device and include entity_id, name, unit, and type.
For one entity's live state, use ha_history_get_state after discovery.

domain.description:
Optional entity domain. Common values: "sensor", "binary_sensor", "person", "device_tracker", "zone".
A one-item array is also accepted for model compatibility, for example ["person"].
Leave empty for statistics-ready entities.

domains.description:
Optional multi-domain live-state discovery. Use for cases like ["person", "device_tracker"]
when looking for person-tracking entities. Do not combine with domain.
Leave empty for statistics-ready entities.

search.description:
Matched against entity_id, friendly name, and device name. Multiple words use AND semantics.
Use for name words like "cave" or "charger", not type words that device_class can express.

area.description: Optional area/room filter such as "Kitchen", "Outdoor", or "Cave".

areas.description: Optional list of areas for one call, for example ["Cave", "Kitchen", "Salon", "Outdoor"].

device.description: Optional device-name filter when the user clearly refers to one appliance or device.

device_class.description: Optional Home Assistant-style device_class filter such as "temperature", "humidity", or "power".

device_classes.description:
Optional list of device classes for one discovery call, for example ["temperature", "humidity"].
Do not combine with device_class.

include_state.description: When true, adds the current state value to each row. Default: false.

json.name: ha_history_get_state
json.description:
Returns the current state of any Oslo entity.
Use after resolving the exact entity_id when the question is about the current state, not history.
Works for all entity domains. Returns the state value, unit, timestamps, and key attributes.

entity_id.description: Exact entity_id resolved earlier. Do not guess.

json.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
json.description:
Computes statistics for one or more instantaneous-value sensors such as temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power in W.
Always pass entity_ids as an array. Prefer one multi-entity call over repeated single-entity calls when units match.
Use aggregations for several whole-period stats in one call. Use interval for time series and group_by for repeating patterns.
Do not use for cumulative consumption in kWh; use ha_history_get_consumption. Do not use for event counting; use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity_ids.description:
Array of exact entity_ids. Use one item for a single sensor or multiple items for homogeneous comparisons.
Resolve IDs first with ha_history_list_entities or ha_history_list_device_entities.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
Single statistic to compute: mean, min, max, median, or count.
Use for time series, group_by queries, or when one whole-period metric is enough.
count requires group_by plus a filter and returns counts per bucket.

aggregations.description:
Several statistics in one call, for example ["mean", "min", "max"].
With interval="none": supports mean, min, max, median — produces a whole-period comparison table.
With interval="hour"|"day"|"week"|"month": supports only mean, min, max — produces a time-series table with one column per entity×aggregation.
With group_by="hour_of_day"|"day_of_week": supports only mean, min, max — produces a grouped table with one column per entity×aggregation.
Cannot be combined with aggregation. Cannot be combined with filter_operator when multiple aggregations are requested.

interval.description:
"none" for one whole-period summary table; "hour"/"day"/"week"/"month" for time series.
Cannot be used with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups by repeating time unit across the full period: "hour_of_day" or "day_of_week".
Cannot be used with interval.

filter_operator.description:
Keep only buckets where the aggregated value satisfies the threshold.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by.

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time series only. Caps rows, not columns. Default: 100. Pass "all" for the full series.

json.name: ha_history_get_consumption
json.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Oslo over a time period.
Use for totals, interval breakdowns, and period-over-period comparisons of cumulative meters.
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id resolved earlier for a cumulative meter. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

json.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
json.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for threshold-based activity questions such as charging sessions, appliance runs, or heating cycles.
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns event count, total duration, a compact session list, or a daily summary with group_by="day".

entity.description: Exact entity_id resolved earlier. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use when daily patterns matter, for example "how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
or "when did charging usually end each day?"
For cross-midnight patterns, combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for overnight device patterns, night shifts, or anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

json.name: ha_history_get_state_history
json.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Oslo.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes: session mode when state_value is set, timeline mode when it is omitted.
Source: HA recorder state history — limited to ~10 days by default.
Returns a timeline of transitions, or session counts and durations when state_value is set.

entity.description: Exact entity_id resolved earlier. Do not guess.

state_value.description:
Target state to detect sessions for.
Binary sensors: "on" (active) or "off".
Person or device_tracker: zone name e.g. "LFO", "home", "not_home".
Prefix with ! for "any state except this one", for example "!home" for time spent outside Home.
Matching is case-insensitive.
Omit to get a full timeline of all state transitions instead.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
